chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about buying the land of the Dhimmis, so he said: There is no problem with it. So it will be, when that occurs, at their status; you will pay from it just as they pay.

He said: And a man from the people of the Nile asked him about a land he bought at the mouth of the Nile, so the people of the land say it is their land, and the people of the Astana say it is from our land. He said: Do not buy it except with the consent of its inhabitants.

key_terms.أَرْضِ الذِّمَّةِ: Land of the Dhimmis (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)
key_terms.بِرِضَا أَهْلِهَا: With the consent of its inhabitants
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهَا: There is no problem with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on buying land from Dhimmis or in disputed territories?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of purchasing 'Ard al-Dhimma' (land held by non-Muslims under Islamic rule), establishing that the buyer inherits the fiscal obligations of the previous inhabitants. It further introduces a crucial condition for contested territories: validity requires the consent of the local inhabitants, reflecting the Shia emphasis on social harmony and preventing dispute (ikhtilaf). This ruling underscores the principle that land tenure is tied to the community's acceptance rather than mere administrative decree.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about buying a land of the Zimmy, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it.
So you would become, when it transpires (rising of Al Qaim<sup>asws</sup>), at their status. You would be paying from it just as they are paying’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And a man from the peple of the Nile asked him about a land bought at the mouth of the Nile, so the people of the land are saying that it is their land, and the people of Al Astana are saying it is from their land’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not buy it except with the agreement of its inhabitants’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about buying the land of tax payers (non-Muslims).
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful. On its coming (the time of the rise of al-Mahdiy with Divine Authority and Power) you will pay what they pay.’

I then asked him (the Imam) about the case of a man from people of al-Nil and a land that he had bought at the outlet of al- Nil about which people of that area said it was their land and people of al-‘Ustan said it was of their land. He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not buy it without agreement of its owner.’”
